name: opencode
one_liner: A free, open-source version of an AI programming assistant that writes and edits code for you from the command line, instead of paying for a closed commercial one.
buyer: An engineering manager at a cost-conscious startup who wants the team to use an AI coding agent without being locked into one vendor's pricing or terms.
business_use_cases: A dev agency standardizes every client project on this instead of a paid tool, cutting software licensing costs across dozens of contractors.
A platform team forks it to bake in internal coding standards and security rules, then rolls it out company-wide as the approved AI coding tool.
A consultancy builds and sells custom agent configurations and prompt packs on top of it for specific tech stacks (e.g. a Rails-focused setup).

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid setup, customization, and training services helping companies adopt and configure it internally.
Build and sell premium plugin packs (custom agents, workflows, integrations) on top of the free core tool.

steal_this: Build and sell one polished, opinionated starter config (agents, rules, integrations) for a specific popular framework, and charge for the setup package.
